open_points.subject: Facts several modules touch, and their one owner
open_points.text: A value of a deterministic backend's IR is held only by the module emitted from it and by no constant: the media types, signatures and download names of `binary_storage` (`rules.binary_delivery_policy`), the table names of the repositories, the hashing parameters of `credential_security`.
open_points.question: Is the backend IR the authoritative owner of each value, with the emitted module merely containing generated code, or does the emitted module own the value despite the IR also recording it?
options: The backend IR owns the value and the emitted module materializes it
The emitted module owns the value and the IR is only generation input
The IR and emitted module are both permitted records
open_points.default_guess: Treat the backend IR as the design-time owner and the emitted module as its generated runtime representation.

witness.initial: A later agent must place a binary media-type signature that `rules.binary_delivery_policy` supplies to generated `binary_storage`.
events: A specification agent decides whether the value belongs to the IR or to the emitted module.
A code agent changes the signature while regenerating or editing the module.
outcomes: The IR is authoritative, so regeneration preserves the changed IR value and overwrites module-local edits.
The module is authoritative, so the value may be edited there while the IR remains different.
witness.observer: A caller receiving a binary whose signature matches one record but not the other

open_points.subject: Facts several modules touch, and their one owner
open_points.text: the table names of the repositories
open_points.question: Are repository table names owned and recorded by `config.persistence`/the persistence backend IR, as the received Persistence and A30 passages say, or held only by the individual emitted repository modules as this passage says?
options: `config.persistence` is the owner and repository modules receive generated literals from it
The persistence backend IR is the owner after consuming `config.persistence`
Each emitted repository module owns its own table names
open_points.default_guess: Keep `config.persistence` as the authoritative record, pass it through the persistence backend IR, and emit repository-local literals without treating those literals as a second owner.

witness.initial: A schema revision changes the table used for one repository.
events: A repository is generated or maintained by a later agent.
outcomes: The repository uses the updated configured table name because `config.persistence` is authoritative.
The repository retains or independently changes its module-held table name because the emitted module is authoritative.
witness.observer: The service or migration opening the SQLite database

open_points.subject: Facts several modules touch, and their one owner
open_points.question: Are the concrete Argon2id hashing parameters values of deterministic backend IR, or are they the pinned hashing library's defaults fixed in source as A30 says, and does “hashing parameters” include the scheme as well as numerical library parameters?
options: The IR explicitly owns every concrete hashing parameter
The emitted module relies on the pinned library defaults and the IR owns only the choice to do so
`config.credential_hash_scheme` owns the scheme while library source/defaults own the remaining parameters
open_points.default_guess: Let the IR specify the Argon2id scheme and reliance on pinned library defaults, without inventing concrete parameter values not supplied by the texts.

witness.initial: The pinned hashing library changes its default Argon2id cost parameters in a Factory-route dependency update.
events: A deployment agent updates the dependency pin.
A code agent regenerates `credential_security` from its backend IR.
outcomes: Explicit IR parameters keep newly generated password hashes on the old costs.
Library-default ownership makes newly generated password hashes use the dependency's new defaults.
witness.observer: Authentication operators measuring or inspecting newly created password hashes

open_points.subject: Facts several modules touch, and their one owner
open_points.text: Every policy value model-written code reads that is the same in every deployment
open_points.question: Who owns a deployment-invariant policy value read by code that is neither classified as model-written nor emitted from a deterministic backend, and what exact criterion assigns a module to either category?
options: All non-deterministic generated modules count as model-written
Only modules whose implementations are produced from prose contracts count as model-written
Such values may remain fixed in manually maintained source
open_points.default_guess: Treat every generated module not emitted from deterministic backend IR as model-written, so its invariant policy values remain data-provider constants.

witness.initial: A manually maintained adapter reads a release-wide closed policy value and has no deterministic backend IR.
events: A specification agent applies the new Data rule.
A code agent chooses where to encode the value.
outcomes: The adapter is considered model-written and imports a typed `data_provider` constant.
The adapter is outside both categories and keeps a source literal with no declared owner.
witness.observer: A maintainer changing the policy value for a later release

open_points.subject: Facts several modules touch, and their one owner
open_points.text: The running service's `adapters/binary_storage.py` still reads the two variables itself until the next Route B regenerates it.
open_points.question: Must code produced from this State 3 already implement the stated emitted-module behavior of calling `load_runtime_settings` at each read, or preserve the direct environment reads until a separately authorized Route B occurs?
options: This State 3 defines the next generated code, so replace the direct reads now
Preserve the running adapter until an explicitly identified later Route B
Describe both implementations as valid during the transition
open_points.default_guess: If this state is used for regeneration, implement `load_runtime_settings` at each binary read; otherwise preserve the current adapter only as documented legacy code.

witness.initial: The process starts with valid binary settings, then its environment is changed before a binary read.
events: The adapter obtains configuration using the implementation chosen by the code agent.
outcomes: The regenerated adapter calls `load_runtime_settings` and applies its validation and `BinaryStorageError` behavior.
The preserved adapter reads the variables directly and follows the old validation and failure behavior.
witness.observer: The binary client and the operator diagnosing the read failure
